text:
ashley_ops: Heads-up — vendor (DeltaShip) just confirmed a regional delay on the EU H100 batch, ETA pushed 8–12 days. They propose splitting the AWB and doing an air-topup for critical units but with a surcharge. Need decision by EOD so they can book slots. :frowning:

mike_procurement: ugh. what's the surcharge numbers? and can we get firm lead times per-serial range?

vendor_ops: Hi all — delta summary from procurement: air-topup adds €1,800 per unit + expedited handling. Partial split available: up to 15 units per AWB. Ground ETA still 8–12d for full batch. We can prioritize serials that hit production tags: S/N starting with EU-PRD.

lucas_logistics: If we split AWB we'll incur extra docs + customs brokerage. likely another €450 handling fee per shipment and potential hold if HS code not pre-filed. Do we have HS confirmation?

ashley_ops: Not yet. @mike_procurement can you confirm HS code (we used 8471.80 before) and ask vendor to pre-file to avoid hold? We also need temporary RMA labels for partial replacements — can't do depot swaps without them.

mike_procurement: pinged vendor for HS confirm and pre-file. also asked for an itemized ratecard and whether surcharge is refundable if they miss revised ETA. waiting on written quote.

vendor_ops: HS code confirmed as 8471.80. Written quote posted here: https://delshp.example.com/quotes/8921 (internal link). Quote includes refundable clause: surcharge refundable if delay >14 days beyond revised ETA.

sara_infra: From infra side — can we route capacity differently? If we get 10 units air-topup we can keep latency SLAs for one critical customer in EU; otherwise we tier them to Dedicated fallback (higher cost but consistent). What's the ops cost of fallback?

lucas_logistics: Fallback routing to Dedicated doesn't solve hardware shortage — it's a customer routing plan. For costs: Dedicated fallback adds ~€0.03/token because model runs move to higher-cost pool. Need decision on which customers to degrade.

ashley_ops: RMA question: vendor can do partial replace but requires photo evidence within 48h and return AWB from depot. If we split, we'll need the RMA label flow automated. @rma_bot can you spin up a temporary RMA workflow for this vendor split?

rma_bot: Created RMA ticket INF-RMA-2026-0048, workflow: partial_air_replace -> photo_upload -> depot_return_label. Deadline for photo evidence: 48h after receipt. Link: https://rma.internal/INF-RMA-2026-0048

mike_procurement: vendor also offered insurance cover for split shipment at 0.6% of declared value. Tradeoff: extra premium vs faster time to market. Thoughts?

ashley_ops: If we pick air-topup + insurance, cost per urgent unit ~€1,812 (surcharge + insurance share). For 10 units = €18.1k. Prospect revenue impact if we miss SLAs is higher, but need product team input. @sara_infra can you quantify likely penalty exposure?

sara_infra: Quick ballpark — two EU customers impacted could face degraded throughput; potential churn risk = ~$60–120k ARR over 3 months if prolonged. Recommend approving 8–10 urgent units for air-topup to buy time.

vendor_ops: If you approve before 18:00 UTC we can lock the air slot and provide final AWB split manifest. We'll attach pre-filed customs docs and courier proforma.

lucas_logistics: Logistics checklist if we split: 1) vendor pre-file HS + commercial invoice 2) courier AWB per partial 3) invoice/credit note for surcharge 4) RMA labels generated and emailed to depot 5) photo acceptance window enforced. I'll prepare a short runbook.

ashley_ops: Action items: (1) @mike_procurement request written quote + refundable clause confirmation (2) @mike_procurement approve insurance optionality (3) @lucas_logistics prepare split-shipment runbook and RMA label template (4) @sara_infra flag customers for fallback plan. I'll consolidate and make call by 17:45 UTC. :ok_hand:
